primary_artifact: /Volumes/HMI-Library/heavy-metal-index-raw/Manual Fetch Kimi /June 3 Folder/Proposition 65 Settlement May Establish New Industry Standard For Lead And Cadmium In Chocolate _ Grimaldi Law Offices _ San Francisco.pdf
disposition_reason: Four-page attorney commentary (30 Dec 2017) describing the proposed Prop 65 settlement between As You Sow and nine chocolate manufacturers. It contains no cocoa occurrence measurements; its only cocoa-relevant numbers are the cacao-percentage-tiered Pb and Cd warning triggers and drop-down levels (ppm), recorded here as regulatory rows.
disposition_locator: article pp. 1-3 (settlement description and Pb/Cd trigger tables)

study.material_scope: chocolate products by cacao percentage (regulatory triggers only)
study.basis: trigger concentrations in ppm, basis not specified (product as sold implied)

controls.control: Industry-wide warning triggers tied to cacao percentage, with automatic drop-down levels and an expert committee to investigate sources and feasible reductions
controls.outcome: No measured outcome. Settlement 'creates incentives for settling defendants to regularly test for the presence of lead and cadmium'; committee to work on a consensus basis and set warning concentrations; maximum settlement payment $210,375 (large grinder/wholesaler with US sales >$500 million).

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary refers to the drop-down as a 'year-7' ladder; the article says levels are reduced 'beginning on the 7th year after the court approves the settlement', whereas the later Expert Committee report (AYS 2022) states the drop-down applies at the sixth anniversary of the Compliance Date (one year after entry); consistent in substance but the stored wording should cite the article's phrasing.

Stored summary says the article documents 'Expert Committee' operation details beyond the text; the article only states the committee works on a consensus basis, is funded by settling defendants and determines warning concentrations - no further details.
unresolved: Article is secondary commentary on a proposed settlement; the entered Consent Judgment text (Feb 2018) was not read here. Trigger values match those quoted from the Consent Judgment in the AYS 2022 Expert Committee report (Attachment 3 s.2.3).
notes: Brand/company names of settling defendants appear in the article (public-record regulatory event); not reproduced in findings. No occurrence data.
